nodes.name: Y-doped RuO2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: K Ru O4 (0.7 mmol) was dissolved in 35 mL of deionized water, labeled as 'solution 1.' Next, 0.3 mmol Y (NO3)3 · 6 H2 O was dissolved in 35 mL of deionized water, after which an H2 O2 (35 wt %) aqueous solution of 2 mL was added to the above solution, labeled as 'solution 2.' Solution 1 was slowly dropped into solution 2 under continuous stirring. The thoroughly mixed solution was transferred into a 100-mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated under 200 °C for 24 h. The dark precipitate was centrifuged and washed three times with water, dried in an oven at 80 °C for 12 h, and the powder labeled as hy-Y0.3 Ru0.7 O2.

nodes.name: Pyrochlore Y2Ru2O7 sol-gel synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol Y (NO3)3 · 6 H2 O and 1 mmol RuCl3 with 8 mmol citric acid were dissolved in deionized water and then heated on a hotplate to obtain dried gel. The gel was calcined at 400 °C for 4 h and then 900 °C for 12 h to obtain the final catalyst.

Υ₀.₃ Ru₀.₇ O₂ exhibited incredibly high OER activity with overpotentials of 170 and 220 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀) and 100 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slopes of 47.9 mV dec⁻¹... overpotential increment of only 30 mV after 300 h, with a degradation rate of 0.1 mV h⁻¹.

PEM electrolyzer loaded with the catalyst shows an outstanding performance with only 1.64 V to reach 1 A cm⁻² and stable operation at 0.5 A cm⁻² over 300 h, demonstrating its outstanding potential for practical applications in PEM electrolysis.
commercial RuO₂ (284 and 590 mV, respectively)... Tafel slope of 74.2 mV dec⁻¹... poor OER stability with the overpotential increasing from 290 to 520 mV after 20 h.
pristine RuO₂ (261 and 434 mV, respectively)... Tafel slope of 62.0 mV dec⁻¹.
The OER performance of the pyrochlore-structure Y₂Ru₂O₇ was also measured for comparison (Figure S27). Y₂Ru₂O₇ exhibited far worse OER activity than Y₀.₃ Ru₀.₇ O₂.
The Y₀.₃ Ru₀.₇ O₂ sample had an ECSA of 223 cm², much larger than that of all the other oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: All characteristic diffraction peaks of ΥₓRu₁₋ₓO₂, pristine RuO₂, and commercial RuO₂ indexed to rutile-phase RuO₂ with tetragonal structure (JCPDS no. 43-1027); peaks broaden with increasing Y content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline structure of the as-prepared Y-doped RuO₂ samples... could be indexed to the rutile-phase RuO₂ with a tetragonal structure (JCPDS no. 43-1027).

nodes.characterization_summary: Commercial RuO₂ shows characteristic vibrational modes E_g, A₁g, and B₂g; ΥₓRu₁₋ₓO₂ shows systematic attenuation culminating in single broadened peak for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy... commercial RuO₂ exhibits characteristic vibrational modes... while ΥₓRu₁₋ₓO₂ (x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) displays a systematic attenuation... culminating in a single broadened peak for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ shows hybrid semi-crystalline architecture with ultra-fine nanocrystals (2.3 nm average) embedded in amorphous matrix, crystalline-to-amorphous ratio 1.54:1, co-existence of low-index (110,101) and high-index (111,200,210) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ adopts a hybrid semi-crystalline architecture comprising ultra-fine nanocrystals (2.3 nm on average) embedded in an amorphous matrix, showing a crystalline-to-amorphous phase ratio of 1.54:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Y cations detected mainly at grain edges confirming Y segregation at grain boundaries (GBs); site-blocking effect impedes grain merging resulting in ultra-small nanograins.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the linescan analysis... Y cations were detected mainly at the edge of the grain, confirming that Y segregation at the interface (GB) of two grains.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM EDX shows Y/Ru ratio ≈ 0.28:0.72 nearly identical to feeding ratio; elemental mapping confirms uniform Y, Ru, O distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental analysis indicates that the ratio of Y/Ru in Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ (Y/Ru ≈ 0.28:0.72) is almost identical to the feeding ratio.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms yield Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 81.3 m²/g for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂, 56.6 m²/g for pristine RuO₂, and 22.8 m²/g for commercial RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms were measured... The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ was calculated to be 81.3 m² g⁻¹, much higher than that of the pristine RuO₂ (56.6 m² g⁻¹) and commercial RuO₂ (22.8 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p₁/₂ peak of Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ shifted 0.37 eV higher than commercial RuO₂ indicating elevated Ru valence; O 1s chemisorbed/lattice oxygen ratio 1.64:1 vs 0.50:1 for commercial.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru 3p₁/₂ peaks of Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ were shifted to a higher binding energy by 0.37 eV compared to that of commercial RuO₂... the ratio of peak area (chemisorbed oxygen/lattice oxygen) in Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ (1.64:1) was much larger than that in... commercial RuO₂ (0.50:1).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR peak intensity at g = 2.003 significantly higher for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ than RuO₂ and commercial RuO₂, confirming enriched oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR peak intensity of Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ at g = 2.003 is significantly higher than that of RuO₂ and commercial RuO₂, confirming the presence of enriched oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows average Ru valence +4.12 in Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂; FT-EXAFS Ru-O coordination number 5.3 (vs 6 for pristine), reduced Ru-O bond length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru K-edge XANES... average valence of Ru in Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ was... +4.12... coordination numbers (CN) of Ru-O for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ was determined as 5.3... much smaller than that for the pristine RuO₂ (Ru-O CN: 6).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms metal composition; Ru dissolution after 300h CP testing: 3.9 ppb for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ vs 6.6 ppb (20h) for commercial RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal component was further confirmed by the ICP-MS test... Ru dissolution... considerably reduced from 6.6 ppb (20 h) for commercial RuO₂ to 3.9 ppb for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂; the latter was averaged over 300 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Thermogravimetric analysis shows 18.7 wt% weight loss to 600°C for Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ under N₂, much higher than commercial RuO₂ (0.15%) and pristine RuO₂ (4.7%), indicating abundant vacancy sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric (TG) measurement... The Υ₀.₃Ru₀.₇O₂ sample exhibited a continuously remarkable weight loss (18.7%) to 600°C under N₂ atmosphere, much higher than that of the commercial RuO₂ (0.15%) and the RuO₂ (4.7%).
